label: Projective 3-Space
notes: Open by framing the chapter as a representation language: every point, plane, line and quadric becomes a homogeneous array whose invariants survive a change of projective frame. Stress that this chapter generalises plane projective geometry, but lines and quadrics behave very differently in three dimensions.

label: Points and Planes in P3
notes: Define the homogeneous four-vector for a finite point and the ideal point with last coordinate zero. Introduce the plane as a four-vector and the incidence equation pi transpose X equals zero. Demonstrate that points and planes are dual: swap their roles and every statement still holds.

label: Projective Transport
notes: Walk through how a four by four collineation H sends points and why planes must use the inverse transpose. Emphasise that incidence is the invariant scalar: it stays at numerical zero before and after the transformation. The notebook audits this with residuals near machine precision and a nonzero determinant.

label: Lines and Plucker Coordinates
notes: Explain why a single cross product fails in three dimensions. Build the skew four by four Plucker matrix from two points, extract the six coordinates, and state the Klein quadratic constraint. Note the dual matrix built from planes gives the same line, the two representations meeting through duality.

label: Intersection and Join
notes: Show how the Plucker matrix L times a plane returns the meeting point, and its dual times a point returns the joining plane. Introduce the bilinear product whose vanishing detects coplanar, hence intersecting, lines. A nonzero value certifies skew lines, as the notebook bar chart confirms numerically.

label: Quadrics in P3
notes: Present the point quadric as a symmetric four by four matrix with X transpose Q X equal to zero, and the dual quadric as the equation on tangent planes. Stress transformation rules: Q maps by inverse transpose sandwiching, the dual by H sandwiching. Both stay symmetric under any collineation.

label: Rank, Signature, Rulings
notes: Classify quadrics by rank and signature computed from eigenvalues. Rank four splits into sphere-type and ruled hyperboloid types; lower rank yields cones, plane pairs, and double planes. Highlight the two families of generator lines on the ruled hyperboloid, every generator point satisfying the quadric exactly.

label: The Twisted Cubic
notes: Introduce the twisted cubic as the curve t cubed, t squared, t, one. Four samples have rank four, so it is not planar. A general plane cuts it in a cubic polynomial, hence three points over the algebraic closure. It is the canonical non-degenerate space curve of the chapter.

label: Plane at Infinity
notes: Identify pi-infinity as the affine upgrade object. An affine transformation fixes it as a set, while a general projective map moves it. Parallel planes meet in a line lying inside pi-infinity. The notebook verifies fixed and moved residuals to separate affine from projective frames cleanly.

label: The Absolute Conic
notes: Place the absolute conic Omega-infinity on the plane at infinity as the metric upgrade object. It has no real point locus, so teach it through polarity and conjugacy: orthogonal directions are conjugate with respect to it. The absolute dual quadric packages pi-infinity and the conic into one four by four object.

label: Transformation Hierarchy
notes: Lay out the four-level hierarchy: projective, affine, similarity, Euclidean. Each level fixes more structure. Affine fixes the plane at infinity; similarity and Euclidean additionally fix the absolute conic. Use this table as the organising map for the whole multiple-view reconstruction pipeline that follows in later chapters.

label: Screw Decomposition
notes: Decompose a Euclidean motion into a rotation about a screw axis combined with a translation along it. Connect this to the metric-upgrade lab: naive transformed normals give wrong angles, while the upgraded absolute dual quadric restores the original cosine. Close by recapping representation, inspection, then invariant.
